The owner also confirms no terminal or hardware access. proposal.problem: The paper claims 99.99% availability for a proposed optical-link terminal over LEO passes, but no hardware, orbital traces, full source text, or defined measurement method are available to the owner.
proposal.question: What observable metric, input data, and measurement epoch would allow a descriptive pilot to record availability-related values for this terminal claim?
proposal.hypothesis: The proposed optical-link terminal maintains 99.99 percent availability over LEO passes.
proposal.conditions: Conditions are unspecified: the pass geometry, atmospheric model, link-margin threshold, and definition of an 'available' interval are all absent from the packet and source metadata.
proposal.related_work: The source citation is synthetic and unreviewed (sha256: aaaa…aaaa); no full text, prior measurements, or comparable terminal studies are available from the packet.
proposal.alternatives: Alternative approaches include: (a) archived simulation or link-budget data if the authors supply them; (b) independent simulation using publicly available orbital ephemeris and atmospheric models; (c) broader validation against published LEO optical-link availability datasets. Each path is distinct and requires separate design review.
proposal.design: No executable design can be drafted until the availability metric definition, input data identity/checksums, and resource bounds are resolved; this proposal documents the gaps and poses the three blocking questions.
proposal.metrics: The primary metric would be an observed availability fraction (dimensionless, 0–1) per LEO pass, with secondary metrics depending on the chosen proxy (e.g., link-margin in dB, handshake success count). Exact bounds are unknown pending owner decisions.
proposal.controls: No controls are defined; candidate controls would include a baseline terminal or a reference link-budget scenario, but none are specified in the packet.
proposal.inputs: No input files, orbital traces, simulation logs, or hardware records are identified; input identity and checksums are unknown and must be supplied by the owner before a protocol can be locked.
proposal.limitations: Hardware unavailability means only simulation or archived-data paths are feasible; simulation results cannot establish real-world performance or generalization. Source metadata is unreviewed and the claim location is synthetic, so published values remain separate from any new measurements.
